thread:
rafa: Heads-up — I ran a short benchmark for llm-7b-v2 (quantized int8) across us-east / us-west / eu-west after yesterday's edge routing tweak. Posting raw snippets and the surprising p95 deltas.

kevin: nice — did you compare A100 vs H100? or just our prod config?

rafa: both. A100 on dedicated-pool-1, H100 on dedicated-pool-2, and a fallback cpu-quant path on t4-like nodes for cold routes. Short command I used: 

rafa: ```
# rbench quick run
rbench run --model llm-7b-v2-int8 --regions us-east,us-west,eu-west --gpus A100,H100 --concurrency 100 --seq 256 --duration 3m --metrics p50,p95,throughput
```

sarah: can you paste the p50/p95 by region? quick table is fine.

rafa: sure. TL;DR: p50 fairly stable (10–18ms token), p95 jumps in eu-west when routed through the new edge pop. Raw (tokens/ms converted to ms per token):

rafa: ```
A100 (us-east):   p50=12ms  p95=28ms  throughput=38 tok/s
H100 (us-east):   p50=10ms  p95=22ms  throughput=44 tok/s
A100 (us-west):   p50=14ms  p95=35ms  throughput=34 tok/s
H100 (us-west):   p50=11ms  p95=26ms  throughput=41 tok/s
A100 (eu-west):   p50=18ms  p95=72ms  throughput=30 tok/s  <-- big p95 tail
H100 (eu-west):   p50=16ms  p95=60ms  throughput=33 tok/s  <-- still high p95
```

gina: that eu-west p95 is concerning. Did you see correlation with routing through POP-B (the new edge pop)?

rafa: yes. I re-ran with explicit routing to avoid POP-B (`--route-policy prefer=primary-pop`) and p95 dropped ~30–40% in eu-west for both GPUs. So it looks network/edge induced rather than kernel.

omar: any kernel differences? flash-attn vs cutlass vs triton? Could perf jitter explain the tail?

rafa: ran kernel toggles on A100 eu-west: flash-attn + cuBLAS gave slightly lower p50 vs triton, but p95 tail persisted until we avoided POP-B. Kernel contrib: ~5–10% on p50, ~10–15% on p95 at most. The big delta was path-level packet loss / queueing at the POP.

bench-bot: Automated check complete. Noted 3% request retries correlating with eu-west POP-B timestamps 1802345600-1802345800.

kevin: good catch. Does the routing change alone buy us steady p95 across regions? Or do we need capacity sizing changes in eu-west?

rafa: two levers: route policy rollback or beef up eu-west edge pool capacity + adjust autoscale thresholds. If we increase reserved workers in eu-west by 20% p95 improves but still worse than us-east. My recommendation: short-term rollback of POP-B route, medium-term increase edge pool and add health checks that detect queueing earlier.

sarah: can you estimate cost impact for adding 20% reserved capacity in eu-west?

rafa: rough calc: current reserved instances 50 A100-equivalent -> +20% = +10 instances. ~ $Xk/mo (engineering will compute exact). I'll drop a spreadsheet.

gina: also, we should add an alert for p95 delta > 2x baseline for >=5min, and automated fallback to alternate pop. Ops? @ops-bot any thoughts on auto-fallback risk?

ops-bot: Auto-fallback enabled in staging. Production rollout requires runbook update. Risk: split-brain routing for sticky sessions if we don't drain KV caches. Recommend canary for 10% traffic first.

omar: are there logs we can attach to the incident page? I want kernel traces + network latency histograms for the p95 window.

rafa: attached small snippets to the thread (screenshot and perf logs). Key lines: 
rafa: ```
[1802345712] pop=POP-B rtt=48ms epoll-queue=12 depth=22 drop=0.8%
[1802345734] pop=POP-B rtt=120ms epoll-queue=60 depth=95 drop=3.1% <-- big spike
```

kevin: thanks. Action items?

rafa: 1) revert POP-B route for 2h canary (I'll open the rollout). 2) increase eu-west reserved capacity by 20% in staging and re-run benchmark. 3) add p95 delta alert + auto-fallback playbook. 4) follow-up kernel sweep but deprioritize until network stable.

sarah: +1 on that plan. Please add timelines.

rafa: plan in prod channel in 10m. will tag owners. :white_check_mark:

bench-bot: Rollout request created: RB-3321 (revert pop-B). CI checks OK.

omar: ping me when you start the canary, I'll tail kernel logs.

rafa: will do — starting at 1802346000 UTC.

gina: thanks for the quick benchmark, raf. Useful to isolate edge vs kernel. :rocket:

omar: nits — for longer runs let's bump seq to 1024 to exercise KV cache effects; short runs underrepresent cache warmup.

rafa: noted. Next sweep will include seq=1024 and a 15m duration.

kevin: great thread. keep the channel posted.
